//devDependencies: prettier, typescript, eslint and the @typescript-eslint pair are pinned EXACTLY rather than ranged. No package-lock.json is committed (.gitignore ignores **/package-lock.json) and every CI job across all 7 workflows runs `npm install`, never `npm ci` — so each run resolves ranges fresh and today's green is not reproducible tomorrow. Prettier ships formatting changes in MINOR releases by policy, so a caret on the formatter alone can turn `quality` red with no code change: `^3.2.5` was already resolving to 3.9.5, seven minors ahead. These are pinned to the versions that were resolving when src/ was formatted. Changing any of them means re-running `prettier --write` and re-checking lint in the same PR. @typescript-eslint stays on v6 (which officially supports TypeScript <5.4, so it warns against the pinned 5.9.3) because bumping to v8 changes which rules fire — that belongs to the lint sweep, not here. vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 are pinned to the SAME exact version for the same reason and one more: the coverage provider is a separate package that vitest loads at runtime, and a caret on the runner would let `npm install` drift it away from the exactly-pinned provider, which fails at load rather than at assert time. Bump the two together or not at all.
